title: Tentacles
body: A ring of stinging arms around the mouth. They fire tiny harpoons called nematocysts to catch plankton and pull it in.

title: Mouth
body: The polyp's only opening. Food goes in and waste comes back out through the same hole.

title: Pharynx
body: A short throat leading from the mouth down into the gut, pulling captured food inside.

title: Stomach
body: The gastrovascular cavity, where food is broken down. It doubles as the polyp's circulation.

title: Septa
body: Vertical partitions dividing the gut. They add digestive surface and anchor the polyp to its stony skeleton.

title: Digestive Filaments
body: Enzyme-loaded threads along the septa. The polyp can push them out through its body wall to digest food outside itself.

title: Gastrodermis
body: The inner tissue lining the gut. It houses the zooxanthellae algae that feed the coral and give it colour.

title: Mesoglea
body: A jelly-like layer between the two tissue layers, giving the soft body its shape and support.

title: Epidermis
body: The outer skin, facing the sea. It secretes the limestone cup the whole colony is built from.
